text: Knowledge, which is the cause of all actions, is of two kinds: memory and experience. Knowledge arising solely from latent impressions is memory. Knowledge other than that is experience. Experience is of two kinds: valid and invalid. When the object possesses a certain characteristic, the experience of that characteristic is valid; for example, the knowledge “This is silver” when the object is indeed silver. This is called valid knowledge (pramā). When the object lacks a certain characteristic, the experience of that characteristic is invalid; for example, the knowledge “This is silver” when the object is actually a shell. This is called invalid knowledge (apramā). ||34||
